title: Merging two copies: union by id, newest `at` per record, `gone` against the same or older `at` only, the hybrid clock, `told` never changing
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 0 and 2.3; DECISIONS_ROUND2 D4, H1, H6, H9
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen).
Times are hybrid clock values written as ISO with the time zone offset (section 0). They are compared as moments, never as text: 10:00+09:00 is 01:00 UTC, 02:30+01:00 is 01:30 UTC.

Question `next_at`: the `at` a device writes, the larger of now and (newest seen + 1 ms), in now's offset. Question `newer`: which of two times is later. Question `merge`: two copies merged, lists ordered by id. Questions `merge_symmetric` and `merge_same`: whether merging A with B gives the same as B with A, and whether merging a copy with itself changes nothing. Question `devices`: a short story of edits and syncs on two devices, and the record one device ends with.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: The clock is ahead of everything seen: `at` is now

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: Now equals the newest seen: one millisecond later
cases.why: max(10:00:00.000, 10:00:00.000 + 1 ms) = 10:00:00.001, so a new write is always newer than anything this device has seen.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: A slow clock: newest seen plus one millisecond
cases.why: This device's clock says 09:05 but it has seen a record at 10:00. max(09:05, 10:00:00.001) = 10:00:00.001, so its edit still counts as newer than what it saw.

cases.question: next_at
cases.title: Two time zones: compared as moments, written in this device's offset
cases.why: now is 01:30 UTC; newest seen is 01:15 UTC, + 1 ms = 01:15:00.001 UTC. now is later, so `at` is now, written with this device's +01:00.

cases.question: newer
cases.title: The later moment can be the smaller text
cases.why: a is 01:00 UTC, b is 01:30 UTC, so b is newer, although as text "...T02:30" sorts before "...T10:00". Comparing `at` as text would let the wrong copy win.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Union by id: a record on each device, both kept
cases.why: Different ids, so both are in the union [D4]. Nothing is dropped.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same record edited on both: the newer `at` wins
cases.why: 10:05 is newer than 10:00, so the copy with 1,500 wins [D4].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The winner's fields, the oldest `told`
cases.why: theirs wins on `at` (10:05), so a is 1,500. `told` is never taken from the winner: the oldest seen for the id is kept, 12:00 not 12:30 [H1, 2.3].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: An Undo newer than the other copy wins
cases.why: The removed copy's `at` (21 Nov 10:05) is newer than the other's (20 Nov 12:00): gone wins, with its goneBy.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: `gone` wins a tie on `at`
cases.why: Both `at` are 21 Nov 10:00:00.000. H6: a copy with `gone` wins against one whose `at` is the same or older, so the removed copy wins before any device tie-break.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A Redo (newer, not gone) wins over the Undo it reverses
cases.why: The Redo cleared gone and goneBy and moved `at` to 10:01, newer than the Undo's 10:00. `gone` wins only against the same or older `at`, so the Redo wins [H6].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Removed on one device, edited later on the other that never saw it: the edit wins
cases.why: H6 as written: the removed copy (10:00) is older than the edit (10:05), so `gone` does not win and the edited record comes back with 1,350. (Open question mg-q4 asks whether that is meant.)

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A removed record on one device only is kept, still removed
cases.why: Nothing is deleted (section 0): a removed record stays in the union with its `gone`, so a third copy that still has it alive cannot bring it back unless that copy is newer.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: The same amount typed on two devices: the merge keeps both
cases.why: Two ids, so both stay. The merge never removes either; the possible double is offered to the person (matching double-01) [H9, 2.3].

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A schedule changed on both devices: the whole newer record wins, the other step is lost
cases.why: "Per record the newest `at` wins" (2.3): theirs (10:05) wins as a whole, so the December step typed on the other device is lost. This is the rule as written; open question mg-q2 asks whether `steps` and `rules` should merge inside the record.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A single record (`home`): the newer `at` wins
cases.why: Single records carry `at` (section 0) and merge the same way: 10:05 is newer, so minBank is null (no minimum).

cases.question: merge
cases.title: A field this page does not know stays on the winning copy
cases.why: theirs wins on `at`; unknown fields are kept (section 0), so `colour` from a newer page survives the merge.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Lists inside the plan merge by id too
cases.why: `plan.budgets` entries are list records with id, told and at (section 0), so they are a union by id like events.

cases.question: merge
cases.title: Two time zones: the later moment wins, not the larger text
cases.why: mine is 01:00 UTC, theirs 01:30 UTC (the laptop is in Europe). theirs is newer and wins with 1,250 (mg-05).

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: Merging A into B gives the same as B into A
cases.why: Every rule above picks a winner from the two copies alone (newer `at`, then `gone` on a tie, oldest `told`), never from which side is "mine". So both devices end with the same copy: e1 removed, e2 at 950, e3 kept.

cases.question: merge_same
cases.title: Merging a copy with itself changes nothing
cases.why: Each record meets an identical copy of itself; any rule keeps it as it is. A merge sent again after a cloud conflict (2.3) therefore cannot change anything twice.

cases.question: merge_symmetric
cases.title: Same `at`, both alive, different amounts: both devices still agree
cases.why: "The device part breaking ties" (section 0) means the tie is decided by something both devices see the same way, so both end with the same record. Which one wins is open question mg-q1; this case only checks that they agree.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A phone whose clock is a day fast does not always win
cases.why: A's clock is a day fast: its edit gets `at` 24 Nov 10:00. B syncs and has now seen 24 Nov 10:00. B's clock says 23 Nov 10:05, so B's edit gets max(23 Nov 10:05, 24 Nov 10:00 + 1 ms) = 24 Nov 10:00:00.001, newer than A's, and 1,800 wins on both devices. The wrong clock did not win [D4]. `told` never moved.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: The same fast phone wins against an edit made without seeing it
cases.why: B edited offline at 23 Nov 10:05 without seeing A's copy, so its `at` is 10:05; A's is 24 Nov 10:00 (fast). A's is newer and 1,500 wins. The hybrid clock means a wrong clock cannot always win (mg-23), not that it never wins.

cases.question: devices
cases.title: A record made on one device and edited on the other keeps its first `told`
cases.why: The record is made on A at 12:00, so `told` is 12:00. B's edit at 18:00 moves `at` to 18:00 and changes the amount, but never `told` (section 0, H1). So a check made at 15:00 that day still holds this spend, wherever it was edited.

open.question: Where is the device part that breaks an `at` tie? A record has no field naming its last writer (the id's device part names the maker, not the editor), and which part wins (larger or smaller) is not said.
open.ref_does: compares the two copies' sorted JSON text and keeps the larger, so both devices agree

open.question: Whole-record wins (mg-15): two devices adding different `steps`, `rules`, `amounts` or `once` entries to one schedule or budget line offline lose one change. Acceptable, or are those lists merged inside the record?
"Every merge moves `at`" (section 0): the copy's `at` and `rev`, or each merged record's `at`? Moving each record's `at` would make the merged copy beat a third device's newer edit.
open.ref_does: records keep the winner's `at`; only the device's newest-seen moves

open.question: A record removed on one device and edited later on another that never saw the removal comes back with the edit (mg-12). Meant by H6?
open.ref_does: the rule as written: the edit wins

open.question: `rev` of the merged copy (2.1 says max(now, rev + 1) on save): from which side's `rev`?
Shared `ui` has no `at` in the shape (2.1). How do two devices' screen choices merge?
open.ref_does: a single object with no `at` is taken from "mine"

open.question: A copy from an older page with no `told` on a record: what `told` does the merge keep?
A device whose clock is far ahead (a year) pushes every later `at` a year ahead for good, on every device. Is there a cap (like the 40 days ahead date check in 2.2)?
